issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException while public constructors and SPI registration still hand out instances.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this. A read-only legacy format that is still publicly constructable and SPI-registered fails at first index flush rather than at construction or compile time. Either remove public constructors, throw from the ctor pointing at Lucene104, or encode read-only-ness in the type (a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat base).

issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT duplicated instead of imported from its canonical source.
issues.detail: The constant was previously imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat; the move introduces a fresh copy with value 16. Two names now point at the same value with no compiler-enforced link, creating drift risk. Either re-import from the original or add a literate comment stating the legacy format intentionally froze its own copy.

issues.description: Constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec that the read-only format silently discards.
issues.detail: The fields were removed but the constructor still takes numMergeWorkers and mergeExec, runs the null-check, then discards both. Parameters that do nothing mislead callers and read like a half-done refactor. Either drop them from the constructor or document explicitly that they are accepted for source-compat and ignored.

issues.description: Protected fields on OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues silently demoted to package-private.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this. The class is still public abstract, so external subclasses lose access without a clear signal. If external extension is no longer supported, mark the class final or sealed; otherwise restore protected. Quietly stripping access modifiers on a public class is an undeclared contract break.

issues.description: Public API surface (NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval) demoted without a deprecation cycle.
issues.detail: Previously public constants and methods on a released format class were narrowed to package-private in the same release that relocates the class. That is an undeclared ABI break for external code referencing these symbols. Leave them public-and-deprecated for one cycle before removal.

issues.description: Patch conflates relocate, visibility narrowing, and write-disable into one commit.
issues.detail: The similarity-index headers make this look like a rename, but real semantic changes (visibility downgrades, writer disabled) are buried inside. Splitting into three commits — pure move, visibility/deprecation, write-disable — would make review tractable and the ABI break visible.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the direction is right — legacy formats belong in backward_codecs and writes should be refused — but the execution mixes a move, a visibility narrowing, and a behavior change in one diff, masking real semantic edits behind similarity-index headers. The main defect is that read-only-ness is enforced by a runtime UnsupportedOperationException in fieldsWriter while public constructors and SPI registration still hand out instances, producing the wrong failure point. Secondary issues cluster around dishonest API shape: constructor parameters silently ignored, a duplicated DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant with no compiler link to its source of truth, and undeclared visibility narrowings on previously public/protected symbols. The fix is to encode read-only-ness in the type, restore or formally deprecate public symbols, and split the patch.
